newsitem.title: UK: UK brokers dissatisfied with Crest says survey.
newsitem.headline: UK brokers dissatisfied with Crest says survey.

text.p: Many stockbrokers remain dissatisfied with the performance of Crest, the London Stock Exchange's new paperless electronic settlements system, said newsletter Securities Interactive in a survey on Monday.

The newsletter said it took a poll earlier this month of the full range of broking groups, from major banks down to small regional stockbrokers. Of the 23 firms who replied 48 percent said they were "unsatisfied", 26 percent were "quite satisfied", 22 percent were "barely satisfied", and one firm was "very satisfied" with the operation of Crest so far.
Securities Interactive said that generally the smaller brokers were mores hostile to Crest than the bigger firms.
"Most common was the opinion that Crest had primarily been designed for major institutions," the newsletter said.
"Scant consideration was felt to have been given to the requirement of small firms or the private investor, who is widely viewed as unready for and distrustful of a 'paperless society'," it said.

Crest's developers decided last month to press ahead with plans to switch the London market over to Crest in April next year, despite calls from some brokers for the transition period to be extended because of fears that it would not be ready by then to cope with busy trading periods.
